# Repo Overview

This repo implements a small TypeScript library that exposes a lightweight bridge between ScriptRunner Behaviours and custom Jira fields.
It is a DOM-focused library (runs in the browser within Jira pages) and is distributed as pre-built artifacts in `dist/`.

**Big picture:**
- Purpose: make custom fields controllable from ScriptRunner Groovy Behaviours by attaching an API to a DOM node.
- Entry points: `VendorsApi.init()` (exported from `src/index.ts` -> `src/api.ts`).
- Internal contract: functions are stored on the field node using jQuery `.data()` and a `data-scriptrunner-vendors-api` attribute (see `src/internal.ts`).

**Key files to read when coding:**
- `src/api.ts` — the public `init` implementation and how the API is attached to a DOM node.
- `src/internal.ts` — constants for `apiKey`, `cfidKey`, `storedValueKey`, helpers like `getField`, `getApiNode`, `getVendorsApi`, and `hasVendorsApi`.
- `src/types.ts` — the `VendorsBehavioursApi` shape and `PromiseOr<T>` usage (important for async/sync polymorphism).
- `__tests__/index.test.tsx` — examples of expected behaviour and how consumers call `VendorsApi.init()` and `getVendorsApi()`.
- `package.json` — build/test scripts, bundling (tsup), published files (`dist/**`) and dependencies.

Project-specific conventions and important details
- The library expects `AJS.$` (jQuery) to be available on the page — this is a Jira environment requirement, not provided by the library.
- When `VendorsApi.init(fieldId, apiSpec)` is called the `apiSpec` object is stored on the jQuery node via `.data(apiKey, apiSpec)` and the attribute `data-scriptrunner-vendors-api="true"` is set — other code looks up the API via `getVendorsApi()` or checks presence with `hasVendorsApi()`.
- API methods use the `PromiseOr<T>` alias: implementations may return a value or a Promise. The public API should accept both sync and async implementations.
- `getValue()` and `setValue()` must be symmetric in the data shape they accept/return.

Developer workflows (commands & environment)
- Install: `npm install` (repo is TypeScript; dev deps include `tsup`, `jest`, `ts-jest`).
- Build (produce `dist/`): `npm run build` (runs `tsup src/index.ts --format esm,cjs --dts`).
- Dev watch: `npm run dev` (runs tsup in watch mode producing dts and bundles).
- Tests: `npm test` (Jest + jsdom; see `__tests__/index.test.tsx` for examples that mock DOM and call `VendorsApi.init`).
- Lint: `npm run lint`.

Testing and debugging notes
- Tests run in `jsdom` (see `jest.config.js` and `jest-environment-jsdom` dependency). Tests mount simple React components that call `VendorsApi.init()` to mimic consumer behaviour — copy that pattern when adding feature tests.
- To reproduce issues locally that require `AJS.$`, either mock `AJS.$` in tests or run in a Jira-like environment; the library itself does not provide a jQuery shim.

Release & packaging
- Bundling is handled by `tsup` and `files` in `package.json` restricts publish to `dist/**`.
- `types` entry points to `dist/index.d.ts` generated by the build. Ensure `npm run build` succeeds and emits types before publishing.

Examples (common patterns)
- Public init usage (see `__tests__/index.test.tsx`):

  VendorsApi.init<string>("customfield_123", {
    setValue: (v) => { /* set DOM input value */ },
    getValue: () => { /* return DOM input value */ },
    setReadOnly: (r) => { /* set readOnly */ },
    bindOnChange: (cb) => { /* store callback and call when input changes */ },
  });

- Internal lookup (consumer code / tests):

  import { getVendorsApi, hasVendorsApi } from "src/internal";
  if (hasVendorsApi(fieldId)) getVendorsApi(fieldId).setValue("x");

Common pitfalls to avoid
- Do not assume `getApiNode()` will always return a plain element — it may return `null`; callers should handle absence.
- Init must be called early — ScriptRunner Behaviours may call your API before the field is fully initialized. Implementations should support `PromiseOr` so the library and Behaviour scripts can wait when necessary.
- Keep runtime side-effect minimal; this library only attaches the API and basic attributes — consumer UI logic belongs in the host plugin.

What the AI agent should do when changing code
- When editing public API shapes, update `src/types.ts`, the implementation in `src/api.ts`, and add/adjust unit tests in `__tests__/`.
- If changing the build output or adding files that must be published, update `package.json` `files` and run the build locally to verify emitted `dist/` artifacts.

Where to look for more context
- `README.md` contains integration notes for plugin authors and example plugin link.
- `__tests__/index.test.tsx` demonstrates expected DOM interactions and is a good source of concrete examples to copy into new tests.
